note: Every module must appear here with a line budget before it is written. Adding a file is an architecture decision, not a convenience.

modules.job: TUNE, MATERIALS, SHAPES, AMMO, PIGS, CARDS, star thresholds. The single source of every number the client, relay and tools must agree on.
modules.budgetNote: Raised from 700 in P3 after authoring the ten underspecified ability and card parameters. Every line added is content plus the reasoning for a number, which is exactly what this file is for.

Raised from 900 after P1. The solver landed at 898 lines against a 900 budget, which is not a coincidence — blank lines between functions had been squeezed out to fit. A budget that buys itself by deleting the comments explaining a sequential-impulse solver is a bad trade.
modules.job: Rigid bodies, sort-and-sweep broadphase, SAT narrowphase with clipped manifolds, sequential impulse solver, position solver, island sleeping, raycast, seeded xorshift. Knows nothing about pigs or scores.

The game on the solver: slingshot launch, critter abilities, material damage, explosions and chaining, pig death, settle detection, scoring, round state, blueprint instantiation, wire format. No DOM, no network, no Math.random, no wall clock.
modules.budgetNote: Raised from 1100 in P3 and from 1400 in P7. It now carries nine critter abilities, four pig traits, four material behaviours, Siege scoring, and the live-world interpretation of the declarative card effects. These all remain one job - the deterministic game on the solver - so it grows rather than splits.

Raised from 1400 in P4 within the editor's explicit 150-line renderer allowance. The added surface is limited to plot/grid, ghost, validation/settle highlights and real-renderer palette thumbnails; any growth beyond this still requires splitting material motifs and pig faces.
modules.job: Canvas 2D renderer. Every pixel drawn in code. Reads world state and the sim event list; never writes to the world. Includes the 260x150 corner preview renderer.
Game-world input, HUD, camera, fixed-step accumulator, editor flow, campaign round flow, and siege match flow. Campaign selection and progress DOM live in campaign-ui.js.
modules.budgetNote: Raised from 1800 for the Siege flow. Siege reuses the editor for its build phase, the round loop for its assault and the renderer's corner preview, and it needs direct access to `round`, the camera, the frame accumulator and the editor's draft. Exporting all of that to a separate module purely to satisfy a line count would have made it harder to follow, not easier.

modules.job: Episode and level selection, ink-drawn star and lock UI, per-level local progress, and non-blocking guard profile merge/sync. Split when the P5 shell would otherwise push game.js past its 2,000-line campaign allowance.
WebAudio synthesis driven by the sim event list. No audio files.
modules.budgetNote: Raised from 200. The estimate predated the event list; there are 15 event kinds plus nine per-ability contours, each needing its own synthesis recipe.

modules.job: Fortress editor: palette, 0.5 grid snap, 15-degree rotation, budget accounting, legality rules including burial depth, settle test, blueprint encode and decode. Produces plain data, never live worlds.
modules.budgetNote: Raised from 600. The estimate predated the legality rules being spelled out: eight validation codes each reporting the offending pieces, a 64-direction burial-depth check, declarative card-effect application, and a bit-packed codec with a legacy path.

modules.job: Parameterized campaign structure generators and the tuple/grid/overlap guards used when composing them. Split from levels.js so 52 level records remain readable data rather than geometry machinery.
modules.budgetNote: Six required structures need independently useful parameters, occupant placement, and collision diagnostics. Keeping those mechanics outside levels.js preserves its budget for the 52 authored level records.

modules.job: 52 campaign levels as blueprint data composed from structural motifs, plus star thresholds. Authored as data and tuned in the editor, not placed by hand in it - see the P5 correction in docs/BUILD_PLAN.md.
Fortress templates scaled to a budget, and a closed-form ballistic aimer with difficulty-scaled noise. Drives solo Siege and the balance harness.
One websocket. Relay resolution order: ?relay= query, window.SLINGWRECK_RELAY_URL, location.origin on localhost, hardcoded workers.dev fallback.

The relay. SiegeRoom and LobbyRegistry Durable Objects, blueprint validation and authoritative settle, shot log, incremental audit replay, preview relaying, reconnect, room passwords, origin allowlist, rate limits.
modules.budgetNote: Raised from 800 across P6 and from 1600 in P7. Two Durable Objects, the full security surface, relay-authoritative build validation, simultaneous Siege and replay, reconnect, plus the best-of-five, loser-only draft, budgets and timeout defaults all remain one authoritative room state machine. The pure audit and match decisions stay split into relay-audit.js.

modules.job: Pure Siege audit engine: deterministic bag generation, unconditional score and shot-timing bounds, incremental sim replay, shot-boundary digest verification, and reconnect snapshots.

tools.job: Seven headless solver assertions: stacking, pyramid, restitution, friction, mass drop, NaN safety, twin-world determinism.
Same seeded scenario in node, chromium, firefox and webkit; compares pose digests after 1800 steps.
Headless rules assertions: launch, damage thresholds, explosion falloff and occlusion, settle detection, scoring.
Renders a deterministic 1280x720 representative fortress frame in headless Chromium.
Playwright solo smoke test through the real UI. Fails on any console error, page error or failed request.
Fires every critter into a standard test fortress, asserts each tap ability measurably changes the outcome, dumps telemetry and screenshots to shots/.
Blueprint encode/decode round trip, legality rule coverage, settle guarantee.
Drive the real fortress editor and capture empty, building, invalid and failed-settle frames at desktop and portrait sizes while failing on browser runtime issues.

Settle selected campaign blueprints through the real simulation, render deterministic 960x540 level frames in headless Chromium, reject blank or errored captures, and build a labelled in-page contact sheet for progression review.

Two directions. Out: encode a level into a copyable blueprint string. In: load level N into the editor for tuning. Also lints every level in levels.js through build.js validate + settleTest, because a shipped level that collapses before the first shot is not a difficulty choice. See the P5 authoring correction in docs/BUILD_PLAN.md.
--campaign flags unwinnable or trivially three-starred levels. --siege runs bot matches across card combinations and flags outliers.
Captures episode select, level grid, and result-star screens at 1280x720 and 390x844, while measuring portrait overflow and rejecting browser runtime issues.
Two real browsers against a real relay through a full round.
A lying client reports an inflated score and must be caught and forfeited.
node --test over the relay's pure helpers: validation, tier selection, seeding, sanitising.
Measured headless Siege rules gate: score components, best-of-five resolution, budgets, seeded loser-only drafts, and one observable before/after assertion for every declarative card effect.
Rewrites the ?v=YYYYMMDD-N cache stamp across every importing file at once; check fails if stamps disagree.
Screenshots a real round into card.png (1000x525) and og-image.png (1200x630), so the marketing image cannot drift from the game.

Checks every level against docs/LEVEL-STANDARD.md by measurement: directly hittable pigs by raycast, gantry share, settled-height monotonicity, two-range count, and stars not set before P5.8. --strict makes it a gate. Written after Episode 1 shipped 8 unprotected pigs that looked fine by eye.
